_source: Promoted from the phase-0 lab corners .scratch/explain-lab-q16-corners.ts (Q16, #185), all 35 of which pass. Expectations are written against the SPEC's requirement, not against observed output: zero false negatives on statically obvious writes, and `unknown` (never `false`) wherever offline cannot prove either answer. Only the ratified `failclosed` navigation arm is pinned; the two arms that priced it stayed in the lab. The corners exist because the corpus cannot reach them — either it has no instances (`source={…}` carrying a write, `:parse`-built commands, `/system/script/run`, `password`, `undo`) or the IL oracle cannot judge them (command text inside a comment or string produces no IL node either way, so `correctly ignored` and `never looked` are indistinguishable at corpus scale).

cases.name: reset-counters — frequency-justified, mutates counters, and the finding-2 shape
write inside a do= block
cases.input: :foreach i in=[/ip address find] do={ /ip address remove $i }

cases.name: write inside the do= of an :if
cases.input: :if ([:len [/ip route find]] > 0) do={ /ip route remove [find] } else={ :put "none" }

cases.name: write inside an :onerror in= scope
cases.input: :onerror e in={ /ip pool add name=p ranges=1.1.1.1-1.1.1.9 } do={ :put $e }

cases.name: bracket find is a READ; block body reads
command text inside a string must not count
command text inside a comment must not count
the OUTER add is a write; the literal source={…} body is not a second one
a write stored in a variable and never run
:parse builds a command offline cannot read
import APPLIES config — a write even though the contents are unknown
:set is a VARIABLE assignment, not a device write
long-tail verb outside the frozen table
singleton verb, plainly mutating, not in the table

_branches: Behavior anchors reaching ratified code paths the oracle-checked corners do not, plus the Q14 floor the production path resolver adds on top of the lab SUT (a structurally defective statement is refused and not descended, so a write may hide in a body that was never walked — it must abstain, not clear).

branches.name: unbalanced delimiter hides an undescended body — abstain, never clear
unterminated string is a document-level note — abstain
empty input has no occurrence to be wrong about
a proven write wins outright over an unknown elsewhere (rule 1)
branches.input:
/ip route add dst-address=0.0.0.0/0 gateway=1.1.1.1
/disk format-drive disk1

branches.name: an unknown poisons an otherwise all-read document (rule 2)
a bare path consumed by a following statement is confirmed navigation
a bare path with nothing after it abstains — /ip/route is a directory but /system/reboot is a write, and the text is identical (Q6 V4)
the case the rule exists for — a lone no-argument write must never clear
an unknown root directive abstains rather than reading as control flow
